html:
Ismail Kadare was the best known Albanian writer, born in 1936 in Gjirokastër, the same stone town as Enver Hoxha.

He studied in Moscow and made his name with The General of the Dead Army, of 1963, about an Italian general searching Albania for the bones of his soldiers. Under the dictatorship he wrote novels such as The Palace of Dreams, a fable of a state that collects and reads its subjects' dreams, which was banned. He lived in a grey zone, both favoured and watched by the regime. In 1990 he sought asylum in France. He won the first Man Booker International Prize in 2005. His work put Albania and its myths, like the Kanun law of the blood feud, on the map of world literature.
